content.title: About
content.content: Red leaf lettuce is a fresh leafy vegetable from the Lactuca sativa species. It features bright red or purple leaves, a crisp texture, and a mildly sweet‑bitter flavor. It is eaten raw in salads, sandwiches, and wraps.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Red leaf lettuce contains more antioxidants than green lettuce thanks to anthocyanins.
Lettuce belongs to the Asteraceae family and is an annual plant.
It is used not only as a garnish but also as a decorative element in many dishes.
Red lettuce can be easily grown at home in pots or containers.
Leaf color can shift depending on light exposure and temperature.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Provides a high amount of vitamin K, essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of vitamin A and folate
items.content: Beta‑carotene and folic acid support vision, cell growth, and immune function.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Contains few calories, making it an excellent choice for weight management.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Anthocyanins and other phytochemicals help combat free radicals.

items.title: High water and fiber content
items.content: Aids hydration and promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Raw leafy greens can harbor Salmonella or E. coli; thorough washing is essential.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some individuals may experience lettuce allergy symptoms such as itching or swelling.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Conventional crops may contain chemicals; choose organic or wash well.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use in fresh salads, as sandwich topping, in wraps, or blended into smoothies. Lightly drizzle with olive oil and lemon juice to enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator in an airtight container or bag with a small amount of moisture. Consume within 3–5 days to retain crispness and vivid color.
